title: Replicating Multi-Agent Failure Taxonomy Across Open-Source vs. Proprietary Model Pairings

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests whether mixed-model multi-agent deployments have different failure profiles. Practically relevant since mixed deployments are common. But the link from failure frequency comparisons to actionable safety improvements is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing a two-agent system in four model combinations, running 5 tasks per combination, and scoring failures against the MAST taxonomy. Multi-agent system setup plus running open-source models locally on medium compute is challenging.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 4 model pairings x 5 tasks = 20 runs, each requiring MAST taxonomy scoring. Plus multi-agent system implementation for each pairing. Too broad for 30hrs.
